data.title: Wall Street fear gauge VIX surges to over four-month high
data.description:
The Cboe Volatility Index surged roughly 30% on Friday afternoon to trade above 21—reaching an over four-month high—amid circulating market rumors that a major hedge fund had collapsed.

After hovering near 16 throughout the morning session, the volatility gauge broke out sharply after midday, rising to an intraday high of 22.31 from a low of 15.73 before stabilizing near 21.43 at press time. The sudden afternoon spike marked a sharp departure from otherwise quiet VIX action.

Market commentators pointed to institutional distress as a potential catalyst for the volatility spike. CNBC options reporter Oliver Renick noted that trading conditions shifted dramatically within a 30-minute window as rumors circulated that a market participant was "getting blown out."

Jim Cramer echoed concerns over forced liquidations, observing that pressure in energy markets alongside "a big hedge fund blowing up" made Friday one of the worst trading days of the year.

Wall Street’s major market averages were markedly lower Friday, with the S&P 500 Index (SP500) down 1.2%, as technology stocks came under further pressure and oil prices extended gains. WTI crude climbed back above $100 per barrel, bringing its five-day increase to about 11%.

data.title: Asked for Diwali sweets, got flooded with costly COD orders: How influencer's viral post turned into delivery nightmare
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 16 -- A festive request made on social media has forced a Madurai-based content creator to leave his home after followers began sending a stream of unsolicited cash-on-delivery (COD) orders to his address.

Veeramani, who is known for his local slang and humorous online videos, had shared his residential address in West Anuppanadi, Madurai, in the hope that a follower would send him a box of sweets for Deepavali, according to PTI.

Instead, some followers allegedly used the address to place a series of COD orders in his name. Delivery personnel from e-commerce platforms such as Amazon and Flipkart reportedly turned up at his residence with expensive electronic items, including washing machines, refrigerators, smartphones and televisions. One television order was reportedly valued at Rs.1.69 lakh.

Veeramani had neither placed the orders nor had the money to pay for them. He therefore could not accept the consignments or share the OTPs required to complete the deliveries.

The pranks reportedly extended beyond household goods. Some users also shared screenshots online claiming to have ordered heavy equipment, including JCB excavators and military tanks worth Rs.70 crore.

Food delivery executives from Swiggy and Zomato also allegedly arrived at his residence with orders placed by others. Distressed by the repeated deliveries, Veeramani posted a video appealing to his followers to stop the pranks. In the video, he said, "I am suffering a lot after requesting a sweet box. Please stop ordering. I am under severe pressure."

However, the deliveries reportedly continued despite his appeal.

When reporters and other social media influencers visited his residence in Anuppanadi, they found the house locked. Neighbours said Veeramani had left the premises after facing persistent harassment from delivery personnel arriving at different hours.

In his latest social media reels, the influencer said, "I am travelling. No one can find my address. Now, no one can control me now." Veeramani's current whereabouts remain unclear, while calls to the phone number listed publicly by him are reportedly being blocked.

When a prank COD order is refused at the doorstep, the shipment is generally classified as a Return to Origin (RTO), meaning it is sent back to the seller.

The seller can incur costs for both the forward delivery and the return journey, despite not completing the sale. According to Amazon Shipping India's guide on RTO, sellers typically bear the cost of both legs of the shipment and do not earn revenue from the refused order.

However, the seller does not necessarily have to absorb every charge. E-commerce platforms may reimburse certain fees depending on their fulfilment arrangements and policies. Amazon India's seller policy, for instance, provides reimbursements for specified charges on undelivered and customer-rejected shipments fulfilled through its Fulfilment by Amazon (FBA), Easy Ship and Seller Flex services.

These include referral fees, while eligible shipping, weight-handling, pick-and-pack and technology fees are also reimbursed depending on the fulfilment model.

The logistics partner is generally responsible for transporting the parcel to the customer and returning it to the seller if delivery is refused. The cost of these services is governed by its agreement with the seller or e-commerce platform.

Amazon Shipping India notes that an RTO can involve forward and reverse shipping charges, along with additional handling costs. Therefore, the courier company does not automatically bear the financial loss simply because the recipient refuses the parcel.

data.title: Kling AI Officially Launches Next-Generation Kling 4.0, Raising the Bar for Professional-Grade Video Models
data.description:
HONG KONG, Oct. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Kuaishou Technology ("Kuaishou" or the "Company"; HKD Counter Stock Code: 01024 / RMB Counter Stock Code: 81024), a leading content community and social platform, today announced that Kling 4.0, the new-generation video generation model of Kling AI, officially launched on October 15.

Kling 4.0's upgrades center on three priorities: realism, control and professional quality. Designed for video creation scenarios featuring intense motion and complex camera movements, Kling 4.0 delivers breakthroughs in three areas: steadier large-scale motion, with smoother continuity in high-speed action and complex camera work; native generation of up to 30 seconds in a single pass, supporting long takes and continuous storytelling with a director's mindset throughout; and Omni Reference, which supports combinations of up to 15 reference assets and up to 10 keyframe inputs, helping creators turn a single idea into a complete work.

Working closely with professional creators to bring their projects to completion, particularly by delivering high-quality key shots, remains a key focus as the Kling model continues to evolve. Professional creators need more than the occasional stunning shot. They need to reliably deliver the key shots that define the quality of their work and bring generated footage into a complete production workflow. Kling AI believes that the value of technology lies not only in enabling content to be generated, but also in making the care behind every frame visible. Whether it's an emotionally charged close-up or a key shot that defines the look and feel of an entire work, every carefully crafted shot deserves to be done justice.

Mastering Both Drama and Action: Steadier Dynamic Motion and Complex Camera Work

Kling AI has long been known for film-grade dramatic scenes, with nuanced, lifelike portrayals of characters' emotions. Building on this strength, Kling 4.0 tackles one of the most common pain points in AI video, delivering more stable and fluid large-scale dynamic motion and complex camera movements. Whether it is high-speed movement and continuous action or sweeping camera movements such as tracking and orbit shots, Kling 4.0 maintains stable visuals and continuity, handling even the most intense large-scale scenes with ease and bringing AI video generation closer to true production-grade delivery.

On the audiovisual front, Kling 4.0 supports output of up to 10-bit HDR, delivering richer color depth and smoother transitions between light and shadow. In high-contrast scenes such as backlit shots, night scenes and neon-lit settings, it preserves greater detail in highlights and shadows, leaving more room for color grading in post-production. Kling 4.0 will also support 4K, 1080p and the 21:9 ultrawide format, further expanding the field of view and compositional possibilities for more immersive and cinematic visuals. For creators who carefully refine their work, these capabilities are more than spec upgrades. They are the foundation for giving key shots a higher level of polish and a more distinctive aesthetic.

For camera direction, Kling 4.0 supports native single-pass generation of up to 30 seconds, supporting long takes and continuous storytelling so that action, scene changes and emotional build-up can unfold in full. Its understanding of camera movements, including push-ins, pull-outs, pans, trucking shots, tracking shots and orbit shots, has been further enhanced, making changes in shot size and transitions smoother and more natural. The model also expands and enriches prompts with a director's eye, while prompt input length now reaches 8,000 tokens, allowing creative intent to be conveyed more fully and precisely.

Flexible Omni Reference: 15 Reference Assets, 10 Keyframes and Video Extension of up to Two Minutes

If 2025 marked the breakout year for AI video generation, 2026 has seen the industry boom. Competition in the field has also shifted from whether AI can generate video at all to whether it can do so reliably and with precise control.

Kling 4.0's upgraded Omni Reference supports flexible combinations of images, videos, subjects and voices in a single task, up to a total of 15 references, including up to 10 images, 5 videos and 7 subjects. These reference inputs work together to keep characters, actions, shots and audio closer to creators' intended results. Kling 4.0 supports a variety of image references, including subject images, three-view character sheets, grid images, storyboards and wireframes, and also allows creators to use video inputs to reference character performance, action, camera movement and narrative pacing. White-model videos and depth-map videos can also be used as references.

Creative recreation has also been upgraded. Creators can draw on the narrative pacing, shot composition and expressive style of a reference video and replace the products, characters and assets within it, quickly turning proven creative ideas into their own content and efficiently producing commercial videos for product advertising, viral social media content, fashion and beauty, consumer electronics and more.

With precise multi-keyframe control, Kling 4.0 supports up to 10 keyframe inputs, allowing creators to freely set key visual moments and precisely specify character states, scene changes and story beats so that content progresses naturally in the intended direction. In addition, the video extension feature will soon support multiple extensions of up to two minutes, giving actions, emotional build-up and multi-part storylines more room to unfold.

Powering Professional Content Creation and Taking Great Stories Global

AI is profoundly transforming production workflows in professional content creation such as film, television and advertising. As generative capabilities continue to improve, the value of AI video tools is shifting from boosting efficiency to enabling professional expression, not only increasing content production capacity but also helping creators consistently bring shots with higher aesthetic standards to life.

Kling 4.0 is also expanding into more creative use cases and genres, spanning film and television, short dramas, animation and advertising. At this summer's Cannes Lions International Festival of Creativity, which incorporated AI into its judging framework for the first time, two works created with Kling AI won Gold Lions, with AI-generated visuals increasingly taking on a central role in advertising storytelling.

In addition, with this major upgrade, Kling 4.0 has been integrated with Kling MCP and CLI, enabling creators to access Kling 4.0 capabilities such as Omni Reference and keyframe-to-video generation through AI agents. Beyond enhancing the user experience, Kling 4.0's model capabilities will soon be made available to enterprise customers and developers through API access, bringing advanced video generation to a wide range of industries.

About Kuaishou

Kuaishou is a leading content community and social platform in China and globally, committed to becoming the most customer-obsessed company in the world. Kuaishou uses its technological backbone, powered by cutting-edge AI technology, to continuously drive innovation and product enhancements that enrich its service offerings and application scenarios, creating exceptional customer value. Through short videos and live streams on Kuaishou's platform, users can share their lives, discover goods and services they need and showcase their talent. By partnering closely with content creators and businesses, Kuaishou provides technologies, products, and services that cater to diverse user needs across a broad spectrum of entertainment, online marketing services, e-commerce, local services, gaming, and much more.

data.description:

Concerns the purported 'energy ceasefire' between Russia and Ukraine has unraveled have also driven crude oil prices sharply higher.

data.description:

data.title: US annual budget gap hits nearly $2 trillion, largest in 5 years
data.description:
Key points:
  • Debt-service outlays climb 12% to record $1.36 trillion, Treasury data shows
  • Net tariff receipts fall $22 billion after $145 billion of refunds
  • Fiscal 2026 deficit equals estimated 6.2% of GDP versus 5.8% in 2025

By Dan Burns

The US budget deficit rose by $217 billion to nearly $2 trillion in the 2026 fiscal year, fueled in part by tariff refunds and record spending to service the nation's more than $40 trillion in debt, marking the largest budget shortfall in five years, Treasury Department figures showed on Friday.

Continued increases in spending for social benefits programs like Social Security and Medicare and a $48 billion jump in defense spending also factored into the increase.

The $1.99 trillion deficit for the year ended September 30, the first full budget year of President Donald Trump's second term, was up from $1.78 trillion in fiscal 2025. It was the largest shortfall since fiscal 2021's $2.77 trillion budget gap, then fueled by COVID-19 pandemic relief spending, and is the third-largest annual deficit ever.

Total receipts for fiscal 2026 were a record $5.40 trillion, up $169 billion, or 3%, from the $5.24 trillion in fiscal 2025. Fiscal 2026 outlays also were a record at $7.40 trillion, up $386 billion, or 6%, from the $7.01 trillion in the prior fiscal year.

Debt-service outlays totaled a record $1.36 trillion, climbing by $144 billion, or 12%, a spending category now eclipsed only by Social Security and the combined outlays for Medicare and Medicaid. Total US debt breached the $40 trillion milestone about two months ago.

Another driver of the widening shortfall was a $22 billion drop in net tariff receipts following a Supreme Court ruling this year negating a large portion of the tariffs Trump had imposed during his first year in office. That triggered $145 billion of tariff refunds over this year, resulting in an 11% decline in net tariff income to about $173 billion.

Defense spending for the year rose by 6% to $917 billion. A US Treasury official said it was not clear how much of the increase could be attributed to the war Trump and Israel started against Iran earlier this year.

The Treasury official said the department calculated an estimated deficit-to-GDP ratio of 6.2% for fiscal 2026, but declined to say what GDP estimate was used. This figure compares to an actual 5.8% deficit-to-GDP ratio for fiscal 2025.

For the 2026 fiscal year's final month of September, the Treasury reported a deficit of $27 billion versus a $198 billion surplus a year earlier.

Zurich and Genoa, Oct 16, 2026 - (JCN Newswire) - Hitachi Energy and Ansaldo Energia today signed a Memorandum of Understanding to develop and market integrated power solutions designed to help customers secure reliable power faster and meet rapidly growing electricity needs with greater flexibility, resilience and speed.

The collaboration aims to bring together complementary capabilities in power generation and power grid infrastructure, combining Ansaldo Energia's gas-turbine and generator technologies with Hitachi Energy's leadership in full grid system integration spanning high-voltage, transformers, automation and power electronics.

Together, the companies intend to develop integrated power generation and electrification solutions capable of serving both 60 Hz and 50 Hz markets, including deployment in data centers.

The collaboration comes as global electricity demand is expected to nearly double by 2050 as electrification accelerates across digital infrastructure, industry, and transportation. The challenge is particularly acute in the United States, where the rapid expansion of AI and data centers is driving unprecedented demand for power and creating an urgent need for reliable, large-scale energy infrastructure that can be deployed faster.

"Power demand is growing at a pace we have not seen for decades as the world enters the electricity era," said Andreas Schierenbeck, CEO of Hitachi Energy. "As power demand continues to outpace available infrastructure, the need for scalable, rapidly deployable power solutions has become increasingly urgent. By combining our complementary strengths with Ansaldo Energia, we help customers unlock new capacity, accelerate time to power, and build resilient energy systems that support economic growth and digital innovation."

"Meeting the world's growing demand for electricity requires closer collaboration across the entire energy value chain," said Fabrizio Fabbri, CEO of Ansaldo Energia. "By combining Ansaldo Energia's power generation technologies with Hitachi Energy's expertise in grid infrastructure, we will provide integrated solutions that accelerate deployment and deliver the scale, flexibility and reliability required by the next generation of industrial, digital and energy infrastructure."

Through this collaboration, both companies intend to develop an end-to-end solution for various applications, integrating power generation with the complete power transmission system through to the point of consumption, including energy hubs, data centers and other large-scale electricity consumers. Hitachi Energy also aims to support the autonomous and integrated operation of data centers through One Hitachi by combining its end-to-end power solutions with HMAX Data Center.

data.title: CBOT soybeans hit 7-week low as drier Midwest weather to speed harvesting
data.description:
Chicago Board of Trade soybean futures fell to a fresh seven-week low on Friday on technical and fund selling and as dry weather forecast over the coming week was expected to accelerate harvesting across the Midwest.

  • The harvest pressure more than offset support from renewed buying by China. The US Department of Agriculture on Friday confirmed private sales totaling 558,000 metric tons of US soybeans to China, bringing the confirmed sales total to China to 1.358 million tons over the past three days. The USDA on Friday also reported 236,000 tons sold to undisclosed buyers, sales which traders said were likely also likely bound for China.

  • A recent stretch of dry weather around the US Midwest has allowed farmers to accelerate harvesting of summer crops, and many growers were gathering soybeans before corn. Midweek rains this week stalled field work, but drier weather is expected through the weekend and early next week, forecasters said.

  • The USDA reported net weekly export sales of US soybeans at 574,000 metric tons in the current marketing year for the week ended October 8, at the low end of a range of trade estimates.

  • CBOT November soybeans (SX26) closed 1-3/4 cents lower at $12.61-1/4 per bushel after earlier touching the lowest level since August 27. The benchmark contract was down 2.4% in the week.

  • CBOT December soymeal (SMZ26) was $2.70 lower at $357.10 per ton.

  • CBOT December soyoil (BOZ26) shed 0.02 cent to settle at 67.13 cents per pound.

data.title: Alkermes reinstated Buy at Truist on narcolepsy opportunity
data.description:
Truist Securities on Friday reinstated its coverage of Alkermes with a Buy recommendation and a $55 per share target, citing the potential of its lead orexin development candidate, alixorexton, against narcolepsy, a sleeping disorder.

Analyst Alex Nackenoff argued that alixorexton has already shown a superior clinical profile against narcolepsy type 1, and its existing data is sufficiently strong in narcolepsy type 2 compared with oxybates.

However, according to Nackenoff, its proof-of-concept data expected from a Phase 2 trial for another neurological sleep disorder known as idiopathic hypersomnia represents the key near-term catalyst for the stock.

“The readout expected toward the end of 2026 presents an attractive risk/reward opportunity; we believe positive data could translate to potentially +20% on the upside with minimal downside risk if negative,” he added.

While Takeda is set to launch the first OX2R product branded as Orzeyful later this year, its opportunity is limited to NT1, according to Nackenoff. "Alixorexton has already demonstrated better efficacy vs. Orzeyful in NT1, and we feel the data is sufficiently strong in NT2 to deliver significant clinical benefit over oxybates,” the analyst added.

data.title: Mexico limits tariffs break to established local carmakers
data.description:
Mexico said on Friday that a new five-year tariff break for imported car parts will apply only to automakers that already have production facilities in the country.

The clarification comes several days after industry analysts raised questions about the decree's potential to open the door to Chinese brands or other newcomer car companies.

  • A decree published Tuesday cut an import tariff to zero from 10% for certain assembly parts, including semi-knocked-down (SKD) and completely knocked-down (CKD) kits

  • The move prompted industry analysts quoted in local media to suggest Chinese automakers such as GAC and JAC could be poised to benefit

  • The economy ministry on Friday clarified that the measure applies only to companies with "productive installations" in Mexico and that meet other specific criteria

  • The ministry said 11 carmakers were eligible under the scheme, without naming them

  • Industry data reviewed by Reuters points to those firms as potentially being Audi, BMW , Ford , General Motors , Honda , Kia , Mazda , Nissan , Stellantis , Toyota and Volkswagen

  • Mexican sales of Chinese-brand vehicles jumped nearly 30% in the first six months of the year despite steep ‌tariffs intended to slow the rise of Asian imports

data.title: Companies Are Saying No to Tokenized Stocks-and Testing Wall Street's Crypto Push — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Joe Light

Crypto firms want to bring stocks to the blockchain, but a growing number of companies want no part of the new "tokenized securities venues."

OKXICE, a joint venture between crypto firm OKX and NYSE parent company Intercontinental Exchange, this week posted a notice disclosing that nine companies have objected to having their stocks traded on its proposed tokenized securities venue. That knocks out about 14% of the 63 stocks that the venture planned to include.

The opt-outs are part of a process established by the Securities and Exchange Commission to allow trading of tokenized stocks.

The SEC last month issued a so-called innovation exemption to let companies offer "tokenized" versions of traditional stocks. The new tokens would trade over blockchains, similar to cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin, but would represent shares of real companies with the same governance and dividend rights.

However, as part of the exemption, the SEC required companies to post a public notice of their intent to launch a TSV and to give firms individually a chance to object to having their shares included on the new platform.

When OKXICE first posted its notice, it disclosed that Cerebras Systems had objected. As of Friday, the objectors also include AppLovin, Applied Digital, Rocket Lab, CoreWeave, Verizon Communications, Applied Optoelectronics, Broadcom, and UnitedHealth Group.

A spokeswoman for networking supplier Applied Optoelectronics said in a statement that the company objected because the framework is new and could have an uncertain impact on its stock's pricing, liquidity and volatility.

"At this stage, we don't see a clear benefit to AOI or our shareholders that justifies these uncertainties, and we will continue to evaluate the framework as it develops," said the spokeswoman, who also said the company did not want investors mistakenly believe that AOI had endorsed the offering.

The other eight objecting companies did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

OKX declined to comment. ICE did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

In an interview with Barron's earlier this month, former New York Governor Andrew Cuomo, who is now OKXICE co-chairman, said that objections from some companies were expected.

"There's going to be a transition period. It's so different. Some companies will jump in. Some will wait and see," Cuomo said.

Though it was never included on the OKXICE list, exchange operator Nasdaq in a FAQ explained why it had planned to opt its own shares out of any of the new securities venues. It said that in deciding whether to opt out, issuers should think about how the venues could "undermine transparent price discovery, fair access to market data, and the safeguards" that some traditional stock market regulations provide.

Company opt-outs might restrict some of the new securities venues, but other stock tokenization projects that don't rely on issuer cooperation are likely to continue apace. Nasdaq itself is among the firms participating in a project by the Depository Trust & Clearing Corp. to tokenize stocks. SEC staff last year issued DTCC a "no-action" letter allowing it to proceed with its project without needing issuers' permission.

Unlike the OKXICE venture, which would allow retail investors to trade tokenized stocks, the DTCC service mostly involves what happens after a trade has occurred. Institutional investors can use the service to transform shares into tokens and then transfer them almost immediately on a 24/7 basis.

data.title: Chip Equipment Stocks Notch Historic Losing Streaks. AI Spending Fears Are Taking a Toll. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Ty Roush

Shares of chip-equipment makers headed for historic losing streaks on Friday, dragged down by concerns about the hot pace of artificial-intelligence spending.

Lam Research fell 3.5% and KLA dropped 2.8%, putting both stocks on pace for their 10th consecutive daily decline. The streaks would be their longest on record. Their shares have plunged 22% and 17%, respectively, over that stretch, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

Applied Materials declined 2.9%. The stock has fallen 22% over the last nine sessions, including Friday, marking its longest losing streak since May 2012.

These companies are big beneficiaries of the AI spending boom because they supply the machinery used to manufacture the advanced chips needed to power data centers and AI systems.

Investors have grown increasingly worried about the financing behind the AI boom, and whether the sky-high spending levels can continue. Those concerns were evident during this month's selloff in bonds issued by CoreWeave, the Nvidia-backed data-center operator.

Yields on some of CoreWeave's bonds surged to levels associated with financial distress, raising questions whether heavily indebted companies can sustain their massive infrastructure investments. Higher borrowing costs could force AI infrastructure developers, like CoreWeave, to scale back expansion plans — potentially weakening demand for advanced chips and manufacturing equipment needed to support the industry's growth.

Earlier this week, CoreWeave told Barron's its revenue backlog, which reached about $104 billion at the end of the second quarter, should more than support payments for all of its debt obligations.

Hotter-than-expected inflation data earlier this week added to pressure on chip-equipment stocks: The fear is the Federal Reserve might increase interest rates to rein in inflation and drive borrowing costs even higher.

The semiconductor industry is also grappling with growing competition from China, after Chinese memory-chip maker ChangXin Memory Technologies announced advances in next-generation memory technology. That offered a reminder that established chipmakers, including Micron and SK Hynix, could lose market share to Chinese rivals.

However, it's important to remember that demand remains strong for chip-equipment makers.

Applied Materials said earlier this week it expects industry spending on chipmaking equipment to grow faster through 2030 than the previous decade. The company stopped short of providing a spending forecast, citing uncertainty surrounding factory construction, supply chains, and infrastructure financing.

Dutch chip-equipment maker ASML offered another encouraging sign. In its third-quarter earnings report on Wednesday, the company said its customers were seeking to place orders for equipment as far ahead as 2030, with its demand to exceed production capacity in 2027 and 2028.

Even with the recent selloff, shares of Lam Research and KLA remain up about 59% and 41%, respectively, this year. Applied Materials is up 64%.

data.title: Cathie Wood Just Sold $7.7 Million of Amazon Stock
data.description:
Cathie Wood's ARK Invest funds sold 30,050 shares of Amazon on Thursday, Oct. 15, generating approximately $7.7 million based on the reported transaction value, as investors continue to assess the costs and potential returns of the company's artificial intelligence investments.

Amazon plans to spend about $220 billion on capital expenditures in 2026, with much of the investment directed toward AI infrastructure, data centers and related technology. The spending outlook has raised questions about how quickly these investments will translate into sustainable cash generation.

The company's latest quarterly results, however, showed continued operating growth. Revenue increased 20% year over year to $200.6 billion in the second quarter, while operating income rose 43% to $27.5 billion, according to its July 30 earnings release.

Amazon Web Services, the company's cloud computing division, delivered one of the strongest contributions. Revenue at AWS climbed 37% to $42.2 billion, marking its fastest growth in 18 quarters as demand for cloud and AI services expanded.

Despite the spending concerns, Wall Street remains positive on Amazon. ARK's sale alone does not establish a change in its broader investment view.

data.title: Bank of America Has Blunt Message on CoreWeave Stock After Selloff
data.description:
Bank of America is standing by CoreWeave after a sharp two-day selloff, arguing that the AI infrastructure company's growth outlook remains strong enough to justify a premium valuation despite mounting concerns over financing.

The bank kept its Buy rating and $140 price target on CoreWeave after the stock fell roughly 18% over two sessions.

Analyst Tal Liani said the decline likely reflected investor concerns around the increasingly difficult financing environment for AI infrastructure companies.

Still, BofA actually raised its revenue expectations.

The firm now forecasts CoreWeave revenue of $26.5 billion in 2027 and $43.3 billion in 2028, up from previous estimates of $26 billion and $41 billion.

That would represent growth of roughly 105% in 2027 and 63% in 2028.

BofA expects CoreWeave to add about 1.4 to 1.5 gigawatts of active power capacity annually over the next two years. Revenue per megawatt could also increase to around $14 by the end of 2028 from roughly $10 today as the company deploys Nvidia's next-generation Vera Rubin chips.

But the expansion comes at an enormous cost.

BofA raised its spending forecasts to $47.4 billion in 2027 and $49.8 billion in 2028.

The bank estimates CoreWeave could spend about $23.8 billion more cash than it generates in 2026 and another $24.8 billion in 2027.

Investor Takeaway

I think this call highlights the central contradiction in the CoreWeave story.

The company's growth outlook is extraordinary, but so are its financing requirements.

CoreWeave has at least $129 billion in contracted backlog, supported largely by major technology customers. Meta accounts for $35 billion and OpenAI another $22.4 billion, while Microsoft's share of backlog has fallen materially, improving customer diversification.

That backlog gives lenders visibility and may help CoreWeave finance expansion.

But investors still have to decide whether enough value remains for equity holders after the debt and capital spending required to build all that capacity.

For investors, the key things to watch are borrowing costs, free cash flow, power capacity additions, revenue per megawatt and whether the backlog continues translating into profitable growth.

BofA clearly believes the answer is yes. The market is becoming much less certain.

data.title: From Verizon to UnitedHealth, Corporate America Is Balking at 'Tokenized' Stocks — WSJ
data.description:
By Vicky Ge Huang

The country's top securities regulator made a push last month to bring tokenized stock trading to the U.S. Now, corporate America is pushing back.

AI chip maker Broadcom, telecom stalwart Verizon Communications and UnitedHealth are among the companies objecting to the Securities and Exchange Commission's plan for tokenizing their stocks, according to a regulatory filing.

Many exchanges and trading venues are eager to offer digital tokens that represent traditional shares and can trade 24/7. The goal is to appeal to a class of new-age investors who have grown up on crypto and want to trade round-the-clock. But some companies worry the SEC's plan for tokenization might create a shadow stock market, distort trading and confuse investors.

And even Nasdaq, which is developing its own tokenization platform, has said it would opt out of having its own shares tokenized under the framework proposed by the SEC. In an FAQ on its website, the exchange operator cited concerns that the plan could create a parallel market outside the National Market System, a series of rules that bind U.S. stock exchanges and help ensure investors get the best available prices on trades on any platform.

"We have determined that our shares should not trade on a venue that does not display best prices in real time, report to the consolidated tape, or provide the transparency investors expect," said a Nasdaq spokesperson, adding that the exchange remains committed to tokenization.

Some Wall Street players warn that the new framework creates hidden risks for public companies. Notices sent by tokenized trading platforms to corporate emails or postal addresses are potentially not actively monitored, and failing to respond within 30 days is treated as tacit consent. Moreover, the framework offers no blanket opt-out, meaning companies will have to monitor and object to every trading venue individually.

The SEC's order last month temporarily exempts authorized trading venues and market makers from certain rules that previously prevented trading in digital tokens that represent shares of listed companies.

But it comes with some safeguards: The tokens permitted by the SEC exemptions will carry the same shareholder rights granted to investors in traditional stocks, including dividend payouts and proxy votes. And before a tokenized securities venue can begin trading any stock, it must give the issuing company 30 days notice. If the company objects, the venue can't proceed with the offering.

The 30-day decision window is rapidly closing for many corporate issuers. OKXICE, a 50-50 joint venture between New York Stock Exchange owner Intercontinental Exchange and crypto exchange OKX, triggered the clock last week when it became one of the first entities to notify regulators of their plans to launch a tokenized stock-trading platform under the SEC's framework.

Nine companies needed little time to make up their mind. In addition to Broadcom, Verizon and UnitedHealth, Cerebras Systems, AppLovin, Applied Digital, Rocket Lab, CoreWeave and Applied Optoelectronics have each opted out.

A spokeswoman for Applied Optoelectronics said the fiber-optic manufacturer objected because it wasn't sure how tokenization would affect its stock price, liquidity and volatility.

"We are also mindful of the risk of investor confusion about AOI's involvement in the offering, which we did not sponsor or endorse," she said. "At this stage, we don't see a clear benefit to AOI or our shareholders that justifies these uncertainties."

OKXICE said it still plans to launch trading for dozens of U.S.-listed companies on X Layer, a blockchain developed by OKX, including Nvidia, Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Tesla, JPMorgan Chase and Walmart.

Andrew Cuomo, the co-chair of OKXICE, has said that he expects some companies to be skeptical and exercise caution about tokenizing their stocks and that is to be expected for any major change. "It is the first step toward tokenizing securities," Cuomo, the former governor of New York, said in a recent interview with The Journal.

Market maker Citadel Securities said in a letter to the SEC last year that the exemptions could facilitate the "emergence of a 'shadow' U.S. equity market" and "allow tokenized U.S. equities to trade completely outside of the national market system." The firm argued that bypassing traditional exchange rules could fragment liquidity, or scatter trading activity across different platforms, and undermine investor protections.

Nasdaq echoed this point, arguing this shadow market "can become disconnected from the broader market in both pricing and price transparency."

Their worries aren't unfounded. Overseas, synthetic tokens, which track stock prices without conferring ownership rights, sometimes deviated significantly from real stock values during off hours and periods of low trading volume. Critics warn that similar risks could emerge under the SEC's framework, including price tracking errors, confusion around proxy voting and dividend distributions as well as legal liabilities for corporate issuers if individual investors suffer big losses in tokens that trade wildly different from the underlying stocks.

Earlier this year, the SEC approved Nasdaq's proposal to allow the trading of some stocks and exchange-traded products in tokenized forms. The exchange took part in a trial run to tokenize securities that Wall Street firms keep at Depository Trust & Clearing, a leading trade processor. It is also working with crypto exchange Kraken and issuing companies in developing its plan to offer tokenized stocks on its exchange.

Brett Redfearn, president of tokenization firm Securitize, said some corporate issuers could object to being listed on one tokenized trading venue without rejecting tokenization altogether. Securitize recently rolled out tokenized stock trading for U.S. investors and the stocks it tokenizes are expected to trade on OKXICE's platform.

Some lawyers note that the SEC's innovation exemptions are a limited experiment to gather information, not a commitment to using this framework permanently. Rodrigo Seira, a partner at law firm Cooley, said the firm has spoken with the agency a couple of times and expects revisions to the current innovation exemptions.

"Part of what they're doing with this exemptive order is trying to get as much information as they can so that they can inform their ultimate rules and make them better, and also make them more defensible from a potential administrative challenge," Seira said.

Write to Vicky Ge Huang at vicky.huang@wsj.com

data.title: Yields on Treasurys, European Government Bonds Edge Higher — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Emese Bartha and Jessica Fleetham

Yields on U.S. Treasurys and European government bonds edged higher on Friday, pulling away from the multiweek lows reached the previous day.

That advance still left yields below the multidecades highs reached last week. Investors have turned their attention away from concerns about inflation and risks of higher interest rates. Now their focus is on the economic impact of high borrowing costs and the sustainability of debt-funded AI investments.

The 10-year Treasury yield traded at 5.123%, up from an intraday low of 5.068%.

Markets priced in 83% odds of an interest rate hold by the Federal Reserve at its Oct. 28 meeting, up from 72% on Thursday, according to CME, following Chairman Kevin Warsh's remarks during an International Monetary Fund event in Bangkok. Warsh stopped short of giving forward guidance, after officials have indicated in recent days that there is no hurry to hike.

U.S. industrial production rose 0.7% in September after an upwardly revised increase of 0.1% in August. Analysts polled by The Wall Street Journal expected a 0.4% increase last month.

The 10-year German Bund yield was at 3.453%, having hit a five-week low of 3.352% on Thursday.

Bond markets face a "rollercoaster ride" of "one step forward, one step back," pulled by changes in oil prices and risk sentiment, Commerzbank rates strategists said in a note.

Since bond yields globally hit multiyear highs earlier this month, investors have been tempted back into buying government bonds again, particularly given concerns about the sustainability of the AI trade.

"U.S. Treasury yields may have reached levels where their elevated levels weigh on risk sentiment," said Jussi Hiljanen, chief rates strategist at SEB.

Investors are also starting to question whether interest rates will rise as much as markets are currently anticipating. Money markets currently price in up to three rate increases by the Federal Reserve and European Central Bank over the next year, and four by the Bank of England, LSEG data showed.

U.S. rates markets are grappling with two key questions--whether the market is pricing in too many interest-rate hikes over the next year and whether bond yields have peaked, Societe Generale rates strategists said in a note.

The risk of energy prices staying elevated and keeping inflation high remains a concern for bond investors, however.

Inflation remains the pivotal variable for markets because it will influence both the direction of monetary policy and the path of government bond yields, said Laura Lake and Tim Crawmer, senior strategists at Payden & Rygel, in a note.

"If inflation cools more decisively, bonds could deliver price appreciation in addition to income," they said.

Oil prices rose on Friday, with front-month Brent crude up 3% at $109.

  • Paulo Trevisani contributed to this article.

data.title: Wall Street tumbles as worries about AI trade and high oil prices weigh
data.description:
Key points:
  • Chips, AI infrastructure companies fall as debt concerns linger
  • S&P 500 and Nasdaq head for steep weekly losses
  • S&P 500 -1.22%, Nasdaq -2.19%, Dow -0.55%

By Noel Randewich and Purvi Agarwal

Wall Street tumbled on Friday, with CoreWeave, Broadcom and other AI-related technology stocks under renewed pressure, while a jump in oil prices spooked traders heading into the weekend.

The Nasdaq was on track for a loss of over 4% for the week, hammered by concerns that debt-laden AI infrastructure companies may not turn profits in time to repay debts, particularly with borrowing costs expected to rise.

Nvidia-backed CoreWeave slumped 12%, bringing its loss over the past five sessions to about 25%. The data center operator's bonds also sold off sharply this week, pushing yields above 15%.

Broadcom fell 3.6%, and the PHLX chip index sank 2.5%, on track for its eighth straight day of declines.

Investors on Friday were also watching oil prices jump more than 3% due to Middle East supply worries.

"There is some fear in the market," said Rob Haworth, senior investment strategist at U.S. Bank Wealth Management in ​Seattle. "High oil prices, in particular, tend to weigh on the price/earnings multiple of stocks, and so I think you have investors looking to be cautious into the weekend rather than take more risk."

Adding to concerns around AI financing, some current Anthropic investors and prospective investors are weighing a lower valuation for the company in its upcoming IPO, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

The S&P 500 was down 1.22% at 7,649.71 points.

The Nasdaq declined 2.19% to 26,128.13 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 0.55% at 51,891.77 points.

Six of the 11 S&P 500 sector indexes declined, led lower by communication services , down 2.52%, followed by a 2.38% loss in information technology .

The S&P 500 was set for its steepest weekly loss since January, and the Nasdaq was heading for its sharpest weekly fall since June.

Third-quarter earnings season shifts into gear next week with reports from Tesla , Meta Platforms and Procter & Gamble . Analysts on average see quarterly earnings surging over 30%, driven by AI-related megacaps, according to LSEG data.

While the S&P 500 remains up about 12% in 2025, most of that gain has come from AI-related tech stocks, and the index’s median component has climbed only about 6%, year to date. About 185 S&P 500 stocks have lost ground in 2025.

Hotter-than-expected consumer and producer inflation reports this week showed price pressures were extending beyond energy commodities.

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh on Friday voiced optimism about US economic strength and surprise about how well global economies have been "hanging in there" during a lingering energy shock and tighter monetary policy to fight inflation.

Markets increasingly expect the Fed to keep interest rates unchanged this month. Barclays now expects 25-basis-point hikes each in December and January.

Tesla dropped 2.5% after the electric-vehicle maker unveiled a redesigned Roadster, powered by rocket-style thrusters, developed in collaboration with SpaceX.

Netflix appointed former Disney executive Peter Rice as chief content officer on Thursday. Its shares were down 2.9%.

Declining stocks outnumbered rising ones within the S&P 500 (.AD.SPX) by a 1.3-to-one ratio.

The S&P 500 posted 19 new highs and one new low; the Nasdaq recorded 49 new highs and 263 new lows.

data.title: Minnesota Records 42 Measles Cases In 2026 As Outbreak Spreads
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - The Minnesota Department of Health said the measles outbreak in Fillmore County, in southeastern Minnesota, has grown to six cases, doubling since the beginning of the month.

The update comes as the state deals with two separate measles outbreaks that began in mid-September in rural Fillmore and Todd counties.

Minnesota has recorded 42 measles cases so far in 2026, already exceeding the 26 cases reported in 2025. In 2024, the state recorded 70 cases, most of which affected unvaccinated Somali American children in the Twin Cities.

'Given how contagious measles is, the case count will very likely grow in the days and weeks ahead,' the health department stated.

According to the health department, all people infected in the recent outbreaks were unvaccinated.

Children in Minnesota are required to receive two doses of the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine before entering kindergarten, unless their families obtain an exemption.

However, the number of kindergartners whose families have claimed non-medical exemptions from vaccination has increased sharply since 2020, reflecting growing concerns about vaccines.

During the 2025-2026 school year, 6.8% of kindergartners in Minnesota had non-medical exemptions, compared with the national average of 4%, according to data from the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

Nationwide, the U.S. has recorded more than 4,000 confirmed measles cases so far in 2026.
